questions.subject: ORGANIC_CHEMISTRY_II
questions.stem: Considering the reaction, which substituent makes phenol more acidic?

options.text: A methyl group para to the hydroxyl
options.misconception: methyl donates and weakens the acid

options.text: A nitro group para to the hydroxyl
A methoxy group para to the hydroxyl
options.misconception: methoxy donates by resonance and weakens the acid

options.text: A tert-butyl group para to the hydroxyl

questions.explanation: Electron-withdrawing groups such as nitro stabilize the phenoxide conjugate base by resonance and induction when ortho or para, lowering the pKa; electron-donating groups destabilize phenoxide and raise it.
questions.hint: Withdrawing groups stabilize phenoxide.

provenance.author: orgchem2-bank-author
provenance.attestation: authored from first principles; no protected content used

questions.subject: ORGANIC_CHEMISTRY_II
questions.stem: Considering the reaction, which structural feature is required for an aryl halide to undergo SNAr addition-elimination?

options.text: An electron-donating group para to the halide

options.misconception: meta cannot stabilize the Meisenheimer complex

options.text: Strong electron-withdrawing groups ortho or para to the halide

questions.explanation: The addition-elimination SNAr mechanism requires electron-withdrawing groups ortho or para to the leaving group to stabilize the anionic Meisenheimer intermediate by resonance; meta groups cannot provide that stabilization.
questions.hint: Ortho or para electron withdrawal stabilizes the intermediate.

provenance.author: orgchem2-bank-author
provenance.attestation: authored from first principles; no protected content used

questions.subject: ORGANIC_CHEMISTRY_II
questions.stem: Considering the reaction, what unusual product distribution indicates a benzyne mechanism?

options.misconception: benzyne gives substitution at either benzyne carbon

options.text: Substitution at the carbon adjacent to the original halogen

questions.explanation: Under very strong base an aryl halide eliminates to a benzyne intermediate, and nucleophile addition to either carbon of the strained triple bond gives a mixture that can include substitution at the carbon neighboring the original halogen, called cine substitution.
questions.hint: Benzyne can give cine substitution.

provenance.author: orgchem2-bank-author
provenance.attestation: authored from first principles; no protected content used

questions.subject: ORGANIC_CHEMISTRY_II
questions.stem: Considering the reaction, why is phenol highly activated toward electrophilic aromatic substitution?

options.text: The hydroxyl donates a lone pair by resonance into the ring
The hydroxyl withdraws electrons inductively only
The hydroxyl is a strong leaving group
options.misconception: that is not relevant to EAS

questions.explanation: The oxygen lone pair donates into the aromatic pi system, increasing electron density especially at ortho and para positions and stabilizing the sigma complex, which strongly activates the ring toward electrophilic attack.
questions.hint: Resonance donation activates ortho and para.

questions.subject: ORGANIC_CHEMISTRY_II
questions.stem: Considering the reaction, which two partners are coupled in a Suzuki reaction?

options.text: An aryl boronic acid and an aryl halide
An aryl Grignard and an aryl halide
An aryl hydrazine and an aldehyde

questions.explanation: The Suzuki reaction couples an organoboron compound such as an aryl boronic acid with an aryl halide or triflate under palladium catalysis and base, forming a new carbon-carbon bond between the two aryl groups.
questions.hint: Boronic acid plus aryl halide under palladium.

questions.subject: ORGANIC_CHEMISTRY_II
questions.stem: Considering the reaction, heating an aqueous acidic aryl diazonium salt gives which product?
questions.explanation: Warming an aqueous acidic diazonium salt replaces the diazonium group with hydroxyl, releasing nitrogen gas and giving a phenol through a carbocation-like intermediate captured by water.
questions.hint: Aqueous diazonium gives phenol.

questions.subject: ORGANIC_CHEMISTRY_II
questions.stem: Considering the reaction, which reagent cleaves an aryl methyl ether to give a phenol?

options.misconception: base does not cleave aryl methyl ethers
that does not cleave the ether

options.text: Concentrated hydrobromic acid or boron tribromide

questions.explanation: Aryl methyl ethers are cleaved by strong acids such as concentrated HBr or by boron tribromide; cleavage occurs at the alkyl oxygen bond because aryl-oxygen bonds are too strong for SN2 attack.
questions.hint: Boron tribromide or strong acid removes methyl ethers.

questions.subject: ORGANIC_CHEMISTRY_II
questions.stem: Considering the reaction, what is the structure of benzyne?

options.text: A benzene ring with an additional triple bond between adjacent carbons
A benzene ring with a radical
options.misconception: benzyne has a strained triple bond

options.text: A benzene ring bearing a carbocation

questions.explanation: Benzyne is benzene with an extra pi bond between two adjacent carbons, forming a very strained alkyne within the ring that is highly reactive toward nucleophilic addition.
questions.hint: Benzyne has a strained ring triple bond.

questions.subject: ORGANIC_CHEMISTRY_II
questions.stem: Considering the reaction, in SNAr on an activated aryl halide, which halogen is generally the best leaving group?

options.misconception: unlike SN1, fluorine is best in SNAr

questions.explanation: In SNAr the rate-determining step is addition of the nucleophile, and the strongly electron-withdrawing fluorine atom stabilizes the Meisenheimer intermediate by induction, making aryl fluorides unexpectedly reactive despite the strong carbon-fluorine bond.
questions.hint: Fluorine is best in SNAr addition-elimination.

questions.subject: ORGANIC_CHEMISTRY_II
questions.stem: Considering the reaction, where is the negative charge of phenoxide delocalized?

options.misconception: phenoxide has resonance contributors into the ring
resonance places charge at ortho and para

options.text: Onto the ortho and para carbons of the ring

questions.explanation: The phenoxide anion delocalizes its negative charge from oxygen into the ring at the ortho and para positions through resonance contributors, which stabilizes the anion and accounts for the acidity of phenols.
questions.hint: Charge appears at ortho and para ring carbons.

questions.subject: ORGANIC_CHEMISTRY_II
questions.stem: In a review problem, which substituent makes phenol more acidic?

options.text: A methyl group para to the hydroxyl
options.misconception: methyl donates and weakens the acid

options.text: A methoxy group para to the hydroxyl
options.misconception: methoxy donates by resonance and weakens the acid

options.text: A tert-butyl group para to the hydroxyl
A nitro group para to the hydroxyl

questions.explanation: Electron-withdrawing groups such as nitro stabilize the phenoxide conjugate base by resonance and induction when ortho or para, lowering the pKa; electron-donating groups destabilize phenoxide and raise it.
questions.hint: Withdrawing groups stabilize phenoxide.

questions.subject: ORGANIC_CHEMISTRY_II
questions.stem: In a review problem, which structural feature is required for an aryl halide to undergo SNAr addition-elimination?

options.text: Strong electron-withdrawing groups ortho or para to the halide
An electron-donating group para to the halide

options.misconception: meta cannot stabilize the Meisenheimer complex

questions.explanation: The addition-elimination SNAr mechanism requires electron-withdrawing groups ortho or para to the leaving group to stabilize the anionic Meisenheimer intermediate by resonance; meta groups cannot provide that stabilization.
questions.hint: Ortho or para electron withdrawal stabilizes the intermediate.

questions.subject: ORGANIC_CHEMISTRY_II
questions.stem: In a review problem, what unusual product distribution indicates a benzyne mechanism?

options.misconception: benzyne gives substitution at either benzyne carbon

options.text: Substitution at the carbon adjacent to the original halogen

questions.explanation: Under very strong base an aryl halide eliminates to a benzyne intermediate, and nucleophile addition to either carbon of the strained triple bond gives a mixture that can include substitution at the carbon neighboring the original halogen, called cine substitution.
questions.hint: Benzyne can give cine substitution.

questions.subject: ORGANIC_CHEMISTRY_II
questions.stem: In a review problem, why is phenol highly activated toward electrophilic aromatic substitution?

options.text: The hydroxyl withdraws electrons inductively only
The hydroxyl donates a lone pair by resonance into the ring
The hydroxyl is a strong leaving group
options.misconception: that is not relevant to EAS

questions.explanation: The oxygen lone pair donates into the aromatic pi system, increasing electron density especially at ortho and para positions and stabilizing the sigma complex, which strongly activates the ring toward electrophilic attack.
questions.hint: Resonance donation activates ortho and para.

questions.stem: In a review problem, which two partners are coupled in a Suzuki reaction?

options.text: An aryl Grignard and an aryl halide
An aryl hydrazine and an aldehyde
An aryl boronic acid and an aryl halide

questions.explanation: The Suzuki reaction couples an organoboron compound such as an aryl boronic acid with an aryl halide or triflate under palladium catalysis and base, forming a new carbon-carbon bond between the two aryl groups.
questions.hint: Boronic acid plus aryl halide under palladium.

questions.stem: In a review problem, heating an aqueous acidic aryl diazonium salt gives which product?
questions.explanation: Warming an aqueous acidic diazonium salt replaces the diazonium group with hydroxyl, releasing nitrogen gas and giving a phenol through a carbocation-like intermediate captured by water.
questions.hint: Aqueous diazonium gives phenol.

questions.stem: In a review problem, which reagent cleaves an aryl methyl ether to give a phenol?

options.misconception: base does not cleave aryl methyl ethers

options.text: Concentrated hydrobromic acid or boron tribromide

options.misconception: that does not cleave the ether

questions.explanation: Aryl methyl ethers are cleaved by strong acids such as concentrated HBr or by boron tribromide; cleavage occurs at the alkyl oxygen bond because aryl-oxygen bonds are too strong for SN2 attack.
questions.hint: Boron tribromide or strong acid removes methyl ethers.

questions.stem: In a review problem, what is the structure of benzyne?

options.text: A benzene ring with a radical
options.misconception: benzyne has a strained triple bond

options.text: A benzene ring with an additional triple bond between adjacent carbons
A benzene ring bearing a carbocation

questions.explanation: Benzyne is benzene with an extra pi bond between two adjacent carbons, forming a very strained alkyne within the ring that is highly reactive toward nucleophilic addition.
questions.hint: Benzyne has a strained ring triple bond.

questions.subject: ORGANIC_CHEMISTRY_II
questions.stem: In a review problem, in SNAr on an activated aryl halide, which halogen is generally the best leaving group?

options.misconception: unlike SN1, fluorine is best in SNAr

questions.explanation: In SNAr the rate-determining step is addition of the nucleophile, and the strongly electron-withdrawing fluorine atom stabilizes the Meisenheimer intermediate by induction, making aryl fluorides unexpectedly reactive despite the strong carbon-fluorine bond.
questions.hint: Fluorine is best in SNAr addition-elimination.
